# Read from the end of an array with at()

Date: 2026-11-22 (Asia/Kolkata)

> Automatically generated by Codex. This is a programming reference, not a record of work personally completed by Abhigyan.

Use `.at()` with a negative index to read items from the end of an array. It leaves the original array unchanged.

```javascript
const steps = ["draft", "review", "ship"];

console.log(steps.at(-1)); // "ship"
console.log(steps.at(-2)); // "review"
```

If the index is outside the array, `.at()` returns `undefined`. It is supported in modern JavaScript runtimes.
